title: A principal nonzerodivisor complement is scheme-theoretically dense
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $a\in A$ be a non-zero-divisor. For the affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme] and the principal open $U=D(a)\subseteq X$ with inclusion $j:U\to X$, the restriction morphism $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective, and $U$ is topologically dense in $X$.

source.place: Tag 07ZU (Divisors, Lemma effective Cartier complement is affine and scheme-theoretically dense), affine-local calculation

proof.text: The map A → A[1/a] is injective by [lem-pc-affine-localization-injective]. Via the natural global-sections isomorphisms Γ(Spec R, ⊤) ≅ R, the map on global sections induced by Spec(A[1/a]) → Spec(A) is injective. Since Spec(A) is affine, its kernel ideal sheaf is determined by its global-sections ideal, which is zero. Thus this map is scheme-theoretically dominant. Identify Spec(A[1/a]) with the open subscheme D(a) using Mathlib basicOpenIsoSpecAway, so the inclusion of D(a) is scheme-theoretically dominant as well. Mathlib Scheme.Hom.app_injective gives injectivity on every open and Scheme.Hom.denseRange gives topological density (the inclusion is quasi-compact because D(a) is affine).
